Second round: summary, 'Measuring tools' concept, point and tip now say level checks level (horizontal) or plumb (straight up and down); no 'flat' wording remains. Re-checked every sentence (wrenches, saws, crosscut vs rip teeth, measuring tools, fasteners, washers/lock washers, pliers, chisels and files). All correct.

problems: Summary: "a level checks whether a surface is flat or straight up and down", concept 'Measuring tools': "A level checks for flat (level) or straight up (plumb).", point: "A level checks flat; a square checks right angles.", tip: "Level for flat, square for corners." Misleading: a level checks whether something is horizontal (level) or vertical (plumb), not whether a surface is flat; a flat board can be tilted. Flatness is checked with a straightedge. Fix: replace 'flat' with 'level (horizontal)', e.g. "A level checks whether a surface is level (horizontal) or plumb (straight up and down)." and point "A level checks level and plumb; a square checks right angles." and tip "Level for horizontal, square for corners."
